lean.fidelity_note: Let $S_\Lambda$ act on $\mathbb T^3=\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$ by the multiplier $\psi(\xi/\Lambda)$. The paper assumes a smooth radial symbol, equal to one on the unit ball and supported in the radius-two ball, and $\Lambda\ge1$. The formal statement permits even symbols and every $\Lambda>0$, and chooses all constants before the frequency, fields and target spaces. It includes the support, parity, divergence, Bernstein and tail estimates. Bernstein's sum counts each multi-index once for every real normed target. The operator bound on measurable $L^\infty$ inputs is stated for complex Banach targets; the real-velocity branch instead assumes continuous inputs. A separate supplied theorem proves the measurable real-velocity bound. Spatial commutation is explicit at every complex order, at first real coordinate order, and at first time order on a smooth closed slab; further real orders require iteration. Thus the paper's smooth-velocity applications are covered, but the literal formal statement combines extensions with differently organized scope. Its supplied description specifies derivative-tensor Hölder norms; their underlying higher-order definition is not included in this packet and has not been independently checked here.
lean.name: TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_B_1

statements.markdown: $S_\Lambda$ multiply the spatial Fourier mode $e^{2\pi i\xi\cdot x}$, $\xi\in\mathbb Z^3$, by $\psi(\xi/\Lambda)$. Subsection 5.7 takes $u=S_\Lambda V$ as the next parent. The frequencies of $u$ are at most $2\Lambda$, and those of $u\cdot\nabla u$ are at most $4\Lambda$. Thus (B.1) bounds derivatives of both $u$ and its residual, while (B.2) controls the error $u-V$.
